# Account security comparison

- Entry ID: quality/account-security-review
- Researched: 4 November 2026; version 1.0.
- Status: historical source review; selected findings are now addressed by the [authorised implementation](../ports-and-adapters/provider-account-security.md). The original observations below describe the reviewed revision, not the current checkout.
- Question: does CEREMO permit self-verification, and which controls demonstrated by the user's named Salesync tenant/account/logout packages are missing or unsuitable?
- Authorisation: the user expressly permitted this read-only Salesync comparison for this task. It does not change the default prohibition for later tasks. Neither application's code or runtime configuration was edited.
- Scope: account identity/activation, tenant provisioning, ownership, logout, transitive security/filter/persistence dependencies and selected tests. This is not a penetration test, deployment assessment or claim that every repository component was audited.

## Evidence and compatibility

CEREMO uses Java 25/Boot 4.1.1, with Spring Security 7.1.1 observed in the built application. The Salesync version catalogue declares Java 25/Boot 4.0.1 and Keycloak admin client 26.0.8. Source was read in the exact local reference checkout identified by the user. No Salesync class/dependency was copied or executed; no source licence was established for redistribution. Its implementation is comparison evidence, not an independent security certification.

| Public primary source, reviewed 4 November | Finding and applicability |
| --- | --- |
| [Spring JWT resource server](https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/servlet/oauth2/resource-server/jwt.html) | Signed-token validation is a security boundary; claim parsing alone is not. Live manual 7.1.2 is ahead of installed 7.1.1. |
| [JwtValidators, Spring Security 7.1.1](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-security/blob/7.1.1/oauth2/oauth2-jose/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/oauth2/jwt/JwtValidators.java), Apache-2.0 | Shows the exact defaults composed by createDefaultWithIssuer. CEREMO adds its audience validator but no required-session/issued-at policy. |
| [JwtTimestampValidator, 7.1.1](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-security/blob/7.1.1/oauth2/oauth2-jose/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/oauth2/jwt/JwtTimestampValidator.java), Apache-2.0 | Default permits absent exp/nbf; short excerpt: `private boolean allowEmptyExpiryClaim = true;`. Checking an existing expiry is different from requiring its presence. No timestamp-bypass exploit was executed. |
| [Keycloak administration](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html) | Documents email verification/SMTP, brute-force protection, administrative roles, events and authentication flows. It does not establish live CEREMO realm configuration. |
| [OWASP authorisation](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html), [REST security](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/REST_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html), [secrets](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html) | Support least privilege, per-request/resource permission checks, bounded requests and externalised/rotated credentials. Recommendations need CEREMO-specific policies and tests. |
| [Spring local logout](https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/servlet/authentication/logout.html), [OIDC logout](https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/servlet/oauth2/login/logout.html), [Keycloak OIDC endpoints](https://www.keycloak.org/securing-apps/oidc-layers) | Distinguish local browser-session logout, IdP session termination and token/session validity. Spring's default /logout is not proof of a product API logout or immediate bearer-token revocation. |
| [OIDC RP-initiated logout, final 12 September 2022](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-rpinitiated-1_0.html) | Logout return locations must follow registered/validated redirect policy. Do not construct a trusted return location from arbitrary Origin input. |
| [Hibernate ORM 7.1 FilterDef](https://docs.hibernate.org/orm/7.1/javadocs/org/hibernate/annotations/FilterDef.html) | applyToLoadByKey defaults false. A query filter is not sufficient evidence of ownership checking on primary-key loads. Salesync's exact resolved runtime behaviour was not executed. |

## Existing CEREMO protections

[SecurityConfiguration](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/shared/authentication/infrastructure/primary/SecurityConfiguration.java) configures signed JWT decoding, issuer/default timestamp checks and audience validation. Private account endpoints require authentication. Browser login has a separate CSRF-protected chain. Shared authentication rejects anonymous/unestablished callers.

[SpringCurrentUser](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/infrastructure/secondary/security/SpringCurrentUser.java) accepts only the exact issuer/subject and Boolean.TRUE email claim from established authentication. [Registration DTO](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/infrastructure/primary/rest/dto/request/RestRegisterUserRequest.java) rejects extra fields. [UserService](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/application/UserService.java) uses only caller identity; [User](../../../src/main/java/io/ceremo/ceremobackend/account/domain/model/User.java) refuses restricted self-reactivation. Database uniqueness, transactions and optimistic versioning remain intact.

No direct unauthenticated or JSON-claim self-verification bypass was found in these paths. Knowing the service logic or calling a public Java method by name does not provide remote execution. Email-based account activation is the user-approved policy; it grants neither a provider verification badge nor provider/staff/subscription privileges. Compromise of the IdP or an authorised administrative credential is a different trust-boundary failure.

## CEREMO findings and proposals

Priorities below are review priorities, not CVSS scores or claims of an observed breach. Checked-in development settings are not evidence of deployed production configuration.

| ID | Priority/status | Evidence, consequence and proposed response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SEC-01 | Urgent; configuration exposure confirmed, credential validity unknown | An admin client-secret literal is present at src/main/resources/config/application.yml:76. The realm export enables ceremo-admin-cli service accounts and gives its service user manage-users/manage-realm. The export masks the client secret, so static equality cannot establish the configured value's validity. No credential was used or printed. Rotate if active; remove the literal and remove/disable unnecessary administrative privileges. Normal JWT validation needs no realm-admin credential. |
| SEC-02 | High; development verification workflow incomplete | Realm verifyEmail=false; VERIFY_EMAIL is enabled but not a default required action. Synthetic pre-verified users exist. Backend verification cannot force the email journey to happen at Keycloak. Configure the intended account flow/SMTP and verify fresh access tokens after actual verification. Disabled verification alone does not make the backend accept false claims. |
| SEC-03 | High before downstream launch; authorisation scope incomplete | API chain generally requires authenticated, with an admin route rule; current self-account lookup intentionally permits own introspection by status. There is no general active-account gate, implemented suspension workflow, provider membership or staff-grant use case. Enforce status plus ownership/membership/specific permission inside each protected use case, with outer method checks where useful. Preserve the plain core. Do not globally ban PENDING users from the activation route or require login for public discovery. |
| SEC-04 | High; product logout/revocation missing | No CEREMO product logout endpoint, application revocation storage/check or coordinated IdP logout was found. Spring's local browser /logout remains available through framework defaults. Local JWT validation does not query current session state; valid stolen tokens can remain usable until the effective expiry/skew window absent another check. Decide and implement explicit logout, restriction and revocation semantics; do not promise instant invalidation merely from browser session invalidation. |
| SEC-05 | High; abuse controls absent in inspected application/development realm | Realm bruteForceProtected=false; no account API rate limiter or explicit registration JSON body-size control was found. Edge infrastructure was not inspected. Require bounded request/identity/verification attempt policies and 429 behaviour before public exposure. Do not invent limits or add an unbounded per-IP map. |
| SEC-06 | High for privileged operations; MFA/recent-auth enforcement not demonstrated | TOTP required action is enabled but not default. That fact alone does not prove MFA absent: an authentication flow could require it. No staff-specific MFA/recent-auth validator is implemented in the inspected CEREMO feature/security code. Demonstrate the intended staff flow and check trusted assurance/freshness for sensitive operations. Do not infer MFA from ROLE_ADMIN. |
| SEC-07 | Medium/high; required-token contract not fully implemented | Document 03 requires issued-at/token/session checks beyond what the local defaults demonstrate. Existing expiry/signature tests do not cover missing exp, required session data, future issued-at or ID-token substitution. Default timestamp source permits missing exp/nbf. Specify the exact accepted Keycloak access-token contract and add appropriate checks/negative tests, preserving issuer/audience/signature validation. No proof was obtained that a live Keycloak user can mint a malformed signed token. |
| SEC-08 | Medium/high; audit evidence incomplete | Realm eventsEnabled/adminEventsEnabled=false. JPA timestamp auditing exists, but no production actor auditor or durable feature security-event history was found. Record attributable activation, restrictions, grants and membership changes with safe metadata, retention and access rules; exclude credentials/tokens and unnecessary personal data. Ordinary updated_at is not an event history. |
| SEC-09 | Required release evidence; not an implemented-feature vulnerability | Actual Keycloak email/refresh/role mapping, JWKS rotation, staff MFA, stolen-token/logout behaviour and production edge limits were not exercised. Sonar server gate and dependency/secret scan execution remain unverified. Coverage cannot prove those behaviours. Add real integration/adversarial cases as each control is implemented. |

## Salesync controls worth learning from

The named account service is itself a short delegate; additional Account/RestAccount fields expose profile/roles/organization information, not an additional verification barrier.

- tenant/infrastructure/primary/rest/TenantResource.java:41 uses ADMIN method authorisation for provisioning/suspension/reactivation; TenantLocationResource.java:35 uses MERCHANT_ADMIN. CEREMO method security is already enabled, but each future privileged operation needs an explicit rule. A class annotation alone does not prove object ownership or protect non-HTTP entry points.
- tenant/infrastructure/secondary/keycloak/KeycloakOrganizationAdapter.java:185-198 creates users unverified and sets UPDATE_PASSWORD/VERIFY_EMAIL. The intended realm journey is useful; CEREMO does not need to copy an admin provisioning adapter for ordinary self-registration.
- TenantProvisioningService assigns organisation membership/admin groups; CEREMO needs explicit provider membership and grant/revoke rules for its own business model. An arbitrary tenant tier/global merchant group is not our billing or ownership policy.
- LocationService/JpaLocationRepository provide findByTenantIdAndId; that scoped-query idea suits future provider-owned records. It is not consistently used by the location ID handlers.
- Tenant.suspend/reactivate and domain events illustrate named transitions and event data; they do not establish that every request is blocked after suspension.
- LogoutResource invalidates a browser session and prepares an IdP logout URL. CEREMO needs corresponding end-to-end product behaviour, adapted to its separated bearer/browser chains.

## Salesync behaviours not to copy

1. The reference SecurityConfiguration disables CSRF on the same chain that supports oauth2Login/browser sessions. Preserve CEREMO's separated browser CSRF protection. This static finding is not a reproduced cross-site exploit.
2. LogoutResource.java:48-56 uses raw Origin in its constructed return URL, manually concatenates query values and invalidates only the HTTP session locally. Provider redirect validation may reject hostile returns; no open-redirect exploit or stolen-token revocation was demonstrated by this code. Use approved registered return URIs/framework logout integration and define bearer behaviour separately.
3. TenantLocationResource.java:91-113 calls unscoped findById/status operations. JpaLocationRepository.java:37 delegates to primary-key lookup; TenantScopedEntity omits applyToLoadByKey. Hibernate's default makes reliance on the query filter insufficient. This is a concrete ownership-control concern requiring a two-tenant runtime regression test; no Salesync tests or attack were executed.
4. suspendTenant saves state and publishes TenantSuspended; the inspected TenantFilter does not load current database suspension status, and no enforcement listener/caller for TenantSuspendedException was found in main-source searches. The documentation's all-access-blocked claim is not established by those paths. Do not treat a state field/event as an enforcement mechanism.
5. provisionTenant performs Keycloak side effects inside a local database transaction without observed compensation in that method. SQL rollback cannot undo a remote organisation/user/group operation. Do not import this workflow wholesale. The adapter's generated-coverage exclusion also conflicts with CEREMO's no-new-exclusion rule.

## Verification and remaining work

Executed in CEREMO only:

```powershell
.\gradlew.bat test --tests '*JwtValidationTest' --tests '*SpringCurrentUserTest' --tests '*UserResourceTest' --tests '*UserActivationServiceTest' --console=plain
```

Result: BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 9s; four suites, 58 tests, zero failures/errors/skips, verified in XML. Tests cover real local RSA signature/issuer/audience/expiry checks, trusted claim mapping, unknown fields, unauthenticated requests and restricted activation. HTTP decoder mocks do not establish live signature validation; the separate crypto tests cover local decoder behaviour. No full build, PostgreSQL rerun, new JaCoCo measurement, Sonar analysis, live credential use, Keycloak API mutation, penetration test or Salesync execution occurred for this review. The prior 512/37 full result and combined coverage report remain historical same-day evidence, not this command's result. The focused test command replaces regular-suite XML/execution data; rerun full check before a later quality claim/analysis.

Remediation order proposed: credentials/least privilege and real realm verification first; required user-token contract and account/staff authorisation next; product logout/revocation, abuse controls and audit; provider ownership/membership before those features launch; actual identity/negative integration tests throughout. Existing shared/wire security, identity, errors, transactions and ID helpers remain the reuse baseline. No new implementation or commercial policy is approved by this review.

Writing/context record: version 1.0, 4 November 2026; local review only, Grammarly pending. No confidential source/draft or credential value was submitted to external services. Public queries contained only generic technology topics. Primary maintainer/standards sources were sufficient; no Medium/LinkedIn/Slack credential or inaccessible conversation is claimed. Product documents 01-09 and private startup files remain unchanged.
